conceptCapsule.title: Angular Momentum Dynamics & Torque Relation
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Definition: For a point mass, angular momentum about origin $O$ is defined as $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = m(\vec{r} \times \vec{v})$. For a rigid body rotating about a fixed symmetry axis, $\vec{L} = I\vec{\omega}$. 2. Torque Relation: $\frac{d\vec{L}}{dt} = \vec{v} \times \vec{p} + \vec{r} \times \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt} = \vec{0} + \vec{r} \times \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}}$. 3. Conservation Law: If the net external torque about a point is zero ($\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$), total angular momentum $\vec{L}$ about that point is strictly conserved. 4. Central Forces: Any force directed along the radial line ($\\vec{F} \parallel \vec{r}$) produces zero torque ($\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \vec{0}$), ensuring angular momentum conservation and constant areal velocity $\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{L}{2m}$ (Kepler's Second Law).
conceptCapsule.examTrap: A particle moving along a straight line at constant velocity still possesses non-zero angular momentum about any origin not lying on its line of motion! The magnitude is constant and equals $L = m v r_\perp = m v d$, where $d$ is the perpendicular distance from the origin to the line of motion.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ is located at $\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ m}$ and moves with a linear momentum $\vec{p} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. The angular momentum $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}$ of the particle about the origin is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \times (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j}) = (3(-3) - 4(2))\hat{k} = -17\hat{k}\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\text{/s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The fundamental dynamical equation connecting external torque $\vec{\tau}$ and angular momentum $\vec{L}$ of a system of particles about an inertial point is:
questions.solution:
$$\frac{d\vec{L}}{dt} = \left(\frac{d\vec{r}}{dt} \times \vec{p}\right) + \left(\vec{r} \times \frac{d\vec{p}}{dt}\right) = \vec{0} + \vec{r} \times \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with an initial velocity $u$ at an angle $\theta$ with the horizontal from the origin $(0, 0)$. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the projectile about the launch point at any time $t$ during flight is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{r}(t) = (u\cos\theta t)\hat{i} + \left(u\sin\theta t - \frac{1}{2}gt^2\right)\hat{j}, \quad \vec{v}(t) = (u\cos\theta)\hat{i} + (u\sin\theta - gt)\hat{j}$$
$$\vec{L} = m(\vec{r} \times \vec{v}) = m\left[(u\cos\theta t)(-gt) + \frac{1}{2}gt^2(u\cos\theta)\right]\hat{k} = -\left(\frac{1}{2}mgut^2\cos\theta\right)\hat{k}$$
Magnitude: $\frac{1}{2}mgut^2\cos\theta$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves along the line $y = d$ parallel to the $x$-axis with a constant velocity $\vec{v} = v\hat{i}$. The magnitude of its angular momentum about the origin:

options.text: Remains constant and equal to $m v d$
Depends on the $x$-coordinate of the particle

questions.solution:
$$\vec{L} = (x\hat{i} + d\hat{j}) \times (mv\hat{i}) = -mvd\hat{k}$$
The perpendicular distance from origin to line of motion is $d$, so magnitude $|\vec{L}| = mvd = \text{constant}$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The angular momentum of a system of particles about a point is conserved if and only if:

options.text: The total kinetic energy of the system is constant
The net external torque acting on the system about that point is zero
The net external force acting on the system is zero
The system is executing uniform circular motion

questions.solution:
From $\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt}$, when $\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$, $\frac{d\vec{L}}{dt} = \vec{0} \implies \vec{L} = \text{constant}$.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The angular momentum vector $\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times \vec{p}$ of a particle is given by $\vec{L}(t) = (4t^2\hat{i} - 2t\hat{j} + 6\hat{k})\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}$. The net torque acting on the particle at $t = 2\text{ s}$ about the origin is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{\tau} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}(4t^2\hat{i} - 2t\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}) = 8t\hat{i} - 2\hat{j}$$
At $t = 2\text{ s}$: $\vec{\tau}(2) = 8(2)\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} = (16\hat{i} - 2\hat{j})\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is executing uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane of radius $R$ with constant angular velocity $\vec{\omega} = \omega\hat{k}$. The angular momentum of the particle about the center of the circle is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{L} = \vec{r} \times (m\vec{v}) = \vec{r} \times [m(\vec{\omega} \times \vec{r})] = m R^2 \omega\hat{k}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The physical dimensions of angular momentum are identical to the dimensions of:
questions.solution:
$$[L] = [r][p] = [\text{L}][\text{M L T}^{-1}] = [\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-1}]$$
Planck's constant $h = E/\nu \implies [h] = [\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}]/[\text{T}^{-1}] = [\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-1}]$.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from rest from point $(d, 0, h)$ at $t = 0$. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the origin $(0, 0, 0)$ as a function of time $t$ is:
questions.solution:
Speed after time $t$ is $v = gt$. Linear momentum is $p = mgt$ vertically downward along $x = d$. Lever arm is $r_\perp = d$.
$$L = p \cdot r_\perp = (mgt)d = mgdt$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A planet of mass $m$ revolves around the Sun in an elliptical orbit. As the planet moves from aphelion (farthest distance $r_a$, speed $v_a$) to perihelion (nearest distance $r_p$, speed $v_p$), the relation between distances and speeds is:
questions.solution:
Central gravitational force produces zero torque about the Sun ($\vec{\tau} = \vec{0}$), conserving angular momentum: $$L = m r_a v_a = m r_p v_p \implies r_a v_a = r_p v_p$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A conical pendulum consists of a bob of mass $m$ rotating in a horizontal circle of radius $R$ with constant speed $v$. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the bob about the center of the circular path is:
questions.solution:
About the center of the horizontal circular track, $\vec{r}$ has magnitude $R$ and $\vec{v}$ is purely tangential ($v \perp R$): $$L = m v R$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: If a central force $\vec{F} = f(r)\hat{r}$ acts on a particle, the torque on the particle about the center of force is:

options.text: Zero, hence angular momentum about the center is strictly conserved

questions.solution:
For any central force, $\vec{F} \parallel \vec{r}$, so $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \vec{0}$. By $\frac{d\vec{L}}{dt} = \vec{\tau} = \vec{0}$, $\vec{L}$ is strictly conserved.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m = 2\text{ kg}$ moves with velocity $\vec{v} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ m/s}$ along the straight line $4x - 3y = 12$. The magnitude of angular momentum about the origin is:
questions.solution:
Perpendicular lever arm distance: $$r_\perp = \frac{|-12|}{\sqrt{4^2 + (-3)^2}} = \frac{12}{5} = 2.4\text{ m}$$
Speed $v = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5\text{ m/s}$.
$$L = m v r_\perp = (2\text{ kg})(5\text{ m/s})(2.4\text{ m}) = 24\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\text{/s}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Kepler's second law of planetary motion (areal velocity $\dfrac{dA}{dt} = \text{constant}$) is a direct consequence of the conservation of:
questions.solution:
Areal velocity is given by $\frac{dA}{dt} = \frac{L}{2m}$. Since gravity is central ($\vec{\tau} = \vec{0}$), $L = \text{constant}$, ensuring constant areal velocity.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with speed $u$ at an angle of $45^\circ$ to the horizontal. The magnitude of the angular momentum of the particle about the point of projection when it hits the ground is:
questions.solution:
Horizontal range: $R = \frac{u^2 \sin 90^\circ}{g} = \frac{u^2}{g}$. Downward landing vertical speed: $v_y = u\sin 45^\circ = \frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}$.
$$L = (m v_y) R = m\left(\frac{u}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(\frac{u^2}{g}\right) = \frac{m u^3}{\sqrt{2}g}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: The position vector of a particle is $\vec{r} = a\cos(\omega t)\hat{i} + b\sin(\omega t)\hat{j}$. The torque $\vec{\tau}$ acting on the particle about the origin is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{a} = \frac{d^2\vec{r}}{dt^2} = -\omega^2\vec{r} \implies \vec{F} = -m\omega^2\vec{r} \implies \vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \vec{r} \times (-m\omega^2\vec{r}) = \vec{0}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating about its fixed central axis with angular velocity $\vec{\omega}$. The angular momentum vector $\vec{L}$ of the disc:

options.text: Lies in the plane of the disc
Is parallel to the angular velocity vector $\vec{\omega}$ along the axis of rotation
Is perpendicular to the axis of rotation
Precesses continuously in the horizontal plane

questions.solution:
For a symmetric body rotating about a principal axis of symmetry, $\vec{L} = I\vec{\omega}$, which is directed parallel to the angular velocity vector $\vec{\omega}$ along the rotation axis.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane with position $\vec{r} = (2t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j})	ext{ m}$. If the mass of the particle is $m = 1\text{ kg}$, the angular momentum about the origin as a function of time $t$ is:
questions.solution:
Velocity: $\vec{v} = 2\hat{i} + 6t\hat{j}\text{ m/s}$.
$$\vec{L} = m(\vec{r} \times \vec{v}) = (2t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}) \times (2\hat{i} + 6t\hat{j}) = (12t^2 - 6t^2)\hat{k} = +6t^2\hat{k}\text{ kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\text{/s}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: If the net external force on a system is zero ($\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$), but the net external torque is non-zero ($\sum \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} \ne \vec{0}$), then:

options.text: Linear momentum is conserved, but angular momentum is not conserved
Angular momentum is conserved, but linear momentum is not conserved
Both linear and angular momentum are conserved
Neither linear nor angular momentum is conserved

questions.solution:
$$\sum \vec{F}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{P}}{dt} = \vec{0} \implies \vec{P} = \text{constant}$$
$$\sum \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt} \ne \vec{0} \implies \vec{L} \ne \text{constant}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A light rigid rod of length $L$ has two equal masses $m$ attached at its ends. It is rotating in a horizontal plane with constant angular speed $\omega$ about a vertical axis passing through its midpoint. The total angular momentum of the system about the axis is:
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia: $I = m(L/2)^2 + m(L/2)^2 = \frac{1}{2}mL^2$.
$$L = I\omega = \frac{1}{2}m L^2 \omega$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.
